# Confidence Intervals in R

We will be showing you how to use R to compute the confidence intervals for a proportion and for a mean.

## Confidence interval for a proportion

A Market research agency interviews a random sample of 1000 people who live in London, and finds that 49% of people suggest they will vote Labour for the London Mayor. Find a 95% and a 90% confidence interval for the true proportion of voters who will vote for a Labour Mayor.

```{r}
prop.test(490, 1000, conf.level = 0.95)
```

95 percent confidence interval:
 0.46 0.52


## What about the 90% CI?


```{r}
prop.test(490, 1000, conf.level = 0.9)
```

The 90% confidence interval is

 0.46 0.52
 
In this case when approximated to 2 decimal places the confidence intervals are almost identical! 

## Confidence interval for the mean

### Reading in from csv - use the skew data.csv

A bit more practice in reading data into R. Make sure you have the skewdata.csv file in the same location as your R project.

```{r}
data<-read.csv("skewdata.csv")
```

## Explore the data

```{r}
summary(data)
```

This data contains only one variable. We can see its mean is 30.969. The minimum value is 4.9 and the maximum is 81.7.

# Visualise the data

It would be a good idea to explore this variable graphcally too:

```{r}
hist(data$values)
```

lets try again, but this time add some more cosmetic changes

```{r}
hist(data$values, main="Histogram of Values", xlab = "Values", breaks= 20)
```

**Which one do you prefer?**

# What is the 95% confidence interval for this variable?

This is looking at the confidence interval for the mean. Therefore we make use of the t.test function in R.

```{r}
t.test(data$values)
```

The 95 percent confidence interval: is 24.11 37.82
 
## We can do the same for the 90 percent confidence interval

This can be done by explicitly stating conf.level=0.9. The default for that value is 0.95.

```{r}
t.test(data$values, conf.level = 0.9)
```
90 percent confidence interval: 25.27 36.66

We can see that the confidence interval is smaller as we decrease our confidence level. 

*Try changing the confidence level again and see what happens?*
